10-1.bio:
The feast of the Protection, or Pokrov, commemorates a vision granted in the tenth century at the Blachernae church in Constantinople, where the robe of the Theotokos was kept. During an all-night vigil, St. Andrew the Fool-for-Christ beheld the Mother of God standing above the people, praying with tears and spreading her veil over the faithful as a shelter.

The feast, kept on October 1 and beloved especially in the Russian and Serbian churches, celebrates the unceasing intercession of the Theotokos, who covers the Christian people with her protection in every trial.
10-1.desc: The Protection of Our Most Holy Lady the Theotokos (celebrated primarily in Russian and Serbian Orthodox Church).
10-1.name: Protection of the Theotokos

10-1.bio:
Ananias was a disciple living in Damascus when the Lord sent him to the blinded Saul of Tarsus. Laying his hands on him, he restored Saul's sight and baptized him, as recounted in the Acts of the Apostles.

Tradition numbers him among the Seventy Apostles and names him the first Bishop of Damascus. He preached in Damascus and Eleutheropolis, where he is said to have ended his life as a martyr.
10-1.desc: Holy Apostle Ananias of the Seventy, first Bishop of Damascus, who baptized the Apostle Paul.
10-1.name: Ananias the Apostle

10-1.bio:
Romanos was born in Syria and served as a deacon in Beirut before coming to Constantinople in the reign of Anastasios I, where he was attached to the church of the Theotokos in the Kyros quarter.

Tradition relates that he had no gift for singing until the Theotokos appeared to him in a dream on the eve of Christ's Nativity and gave him a scroll to eat; he then chanted the kontakion 'Today the Virgin gives birth to the Transcendent One.' He went on to compose a vast number of kontakia and is honored as the patron of church chanters.
10-1.desc: Venerable Romanos the Melodist, deacon of Constantinople and the greatest of Byzantine hymnographers.
10-1.name: Romanos the Melodist

10-1.bio:
John was born at Dyrrachion and, orphaned young, was taken into the imperial school of Constantinople for his remarkable voice, becoming the chief court singer. Longing for the monastic life, he fled secretly to the Great Lavra of Mount Athos, where he at first hid his identity and tended the goats.

Once recognized, he was allowed to remain and devoted himself to chanting and composition, becoming one of the chief masters of Byzantine music. Tradition relates that the Theotokos appeared to him after an all-night vigil and placed a gold coin in his hand in gratitude for his singing.
10-1.desc: Venerable John Koukouzelis, the master chanter of the Great Lavra on Mount Athos.
10-1.name: John Koukouzelis

10-1.bio:
Michael was abbot of the monastery of Zobe near Sebasteia in Armenia in the eighth century, during the reign of Constantine VI. When Saracen raiders overran the region, the abbot and thirty-six of his monks were seized and ordered to renounce Christ.

All refused and were put to the sword, sealing their monastic struggle with the crown of martyrdom.
10-1.desc: Holy Monk-Martyr Michael, Abbot of the Zobe monastery near Sebasteia, and the thirty-six fathers martyred with him.
10-1.name: Michael of Zobe and the 36 Monk-Martyrs

10-1.bio:
Domninos was a Christian of Thessalonica who openly confessed Christ when the emperor Maximian was residing in the city. Brought before him, he refused to sacrifice to the idols and was cruelly tortured.

Tradition relates that his legs were broken and he was left outside the city, where after some days he gave up his soul to God around the end of the third century.
10-1.desc: Holy Martyr Domninos, who suffered at Thessalonica under Maximian.
10-1.name: Domninos of Thessalonica

10-10.bio:
Saints Eulampios and Eulampia were brother and sister, Christians of Nicomedia during the persecution under the Emperor Maximian at the beginning of the fourth century. When Eulampios was seized and tortured for confessing Christ, his sister Eulampia openly declared her own faith so that she might share his sufferings, and together they endured torment and received the crown of martyrdom.

Their courage moved many who witnessed it to believe in Christ. The two siblings are commemorated together on October 10.
10-10.name: Eulampios and Eulampia

10-10.bio:
Theophilos the Confessor and Longinus the Stylite are commemorated together in the Synaxarion of this day. Theophilos suffered for the holy icons, and Longinus lived in asceticism upon a pillar.

The Church honors them among the venerable fathers who bore witness by confession and ascetic struggle.
10-10.desc: Venerable Theophilos the Confessor and Longinus the Stylite.
10-10.name: Theophilos and Longinus the Stylite

10-10.bio:
Bassianos came from Syria to Constantinople in the reign of the emperor Marcian and built a monastery where some three hundred monks gathered under his rule. He was honored by the emperor and the empress Pulcheria.

He worked miracles during his life, and Saint Matrona of Perge was among his disciples; he reposed in peace in the fifth century.
10-10.desc: Venerable Bassianos, ascetic of Syria who founded a great monastery in Constantinople.
10-10.name: Bassianos of Constantinople

10-10.bio:
Born Alexander Grenkov in 1812, he entered Optina after a vow made in illness and became the disciple of the elders Leonid and Macarius. Despite lifelong sickness he received thousands of pilgrims, giving counsel marked by warmth and humor.

He founded the Shamordino convent and reposed in 1891; he was glorified in 1988 and is one of the most beloved of the Optina elders.
10-10.desc: Venerable Ambrose, the great elder of Optina Monastery.
10-10.name: Ambrose of Optina

10-10.bio:
When the emperor Michael VIII Palaiologos tried to impose union with Rome, Latin troops came to the Holy Mountain to force the monks to submit. Twenty-six fathers of the Bulgarian monastery of Zographou, led by the abbot Thomas, refused and shut themselves in the tower.

The tower was set on fire and they perished confessing the Orthodox faith. Tradition relates that the Theotokos had forewarned them through her icon, which was preserved unharmed.
10-10.desc: The twenty-six Monk-Martyrs of Zographou Monastery on Mount Athos, burned by the Latinizers in 1276.
10-10.name: Twenty-six Martyrs of Zographou

10-10.bio:
Andrew was born in 1638 near Totma in northern Russia and from youth took up the ascetic path of foolishness for Christ under the blessing of a monastic elder. He lived by a church in Totma, going barefoot in winter and giving away all he received.

He reposed in 1673, and tradition relates many healings at his tomb.
10-10.desc: Blessed Andrew of Totma, fool for Christ.
10-10.name: Andrew of Totma

10-11.bio:
St. Philip was one of the seven deacons chosen by the apostles to serve the early Church in Jerusalem, as the Acts of the Apostles relates. Full of the Holy Spirit, he preached Christ in Samaria with great power, and on the desert road he baptized the Ethiopian eunuch, opening the Gospel to the nations.

Tradition relates that he continued his apostolic labors and served the Church as a bishop in Asia Minor, where his daughters also were known for the gift of prophecy. He is commemorated on October 11.
10-11.desc: Holy Apostle Philip of the Seven Deacons.
10-11.name: Philip the Apostle (Deacon)

10-11.bio:
In 787, under the empress Irene and Patriarch Tarasios, some three hundred and fifty bishops gathered at Nicaea and condemned the iconoclast heresy. They declared that the honor given to an icon passes to its prototype, and that icons of Christ, the Theotokos and the saints are to be venerated but not worshipped.

The Church commemorates these Fathers on the Sunday falling on or after October 11.
10-11.desc: Commemoration of the Holy Fathers of the Seventh Ecumenical Council at Nicaea, which upheld the veneration of the holy icons.
10-11.name: Fathers of the Seventh Ecumenical Council

10-11.bio:
Theophanes and his elder brother Theodore, monks of the Lavra of Saint Sabbas in Palestine, were sent to Constantinople to defend the holy icons. The iconoclast emperor Theophilos had insulting verses tattooed on their faces, whence their name the Branded, and sent them into exile.

After the restoration of the icons Theophanes was made Bishop of Nicaea. He composed many canons and reposed in peace around 847.
10-11.desc: Saint Theophanes the Confessor and Hymnographer, Bishop of Nicaea, called the Branded.
10-11.name: Theophanes the Branded

10-11.bio:
Nektarios, a senator of Tarsus, was chosen Patriarch while still a catechumen and presided at the Second Ecumenical Council in 381, reposing in 397. Arsakios, the brother of Nektarios, briefly held the throne after the exile of Saint John Chrysostom.

Sisinios, Patriarch from 426 to 427, was renowned for his almsgiving and purity of life. The Church commemorates the three hierarchs together.
10-11.desc: Saints Nektarios, Arsakios and Sisinios, Patriarchs of Constantinople.
10-11.name: Nektarios, Arsakios and Sisinios of Constantinople

10-11.bio:
Zenaida and Philonilla were sisters from Tarsus in Cilicia, related to the Apostle Paul, who studied medicine and used their art to serve the sick freely in the name of Christ.

They settled in a cave near Demetrias in Thessaly, healing the bodies and souls of those who came to them, and reposed in peace in the first century.
10-11.desc: Holy Women Zenaida and Philonilla of Tarsus, physicians and kinswomen of the Apostle Paul.
10-11.name: Zenaida and Philonilla

10-11.bio:
Philotheos was born in Thessalonica and became a monk on Mount Athos, where he was abbot of the Great Lavra and a close friend of Saint Gregory Palamas. He served as Metropolitan of Heraclea and twice as Patriarch of Constantinople in the fourteenth century.

He presided over the council that confirmed the teaching of Palamas, composed his life and service, and wrote many hymns and theological works before reposing around 1379.
10-11.desc: Saint Philotheos Kokkinos, Patriarch of Constantinople, defender of the hesychasts.
10-11.name: Philotheos Kokkinos

10-11.bio:
Jonas was a Cypriot ascetic who, tradition relates, lived near the village of Pergamos in the Larnaca district. He is remembered as a disciple and companion of Saint John Lampadistis and a man of prayer and miracles.

His memory is kept especially in the churches of Cyprus that bear his name.
10-11.desc: Venerable Jonas of Pergamos in Cyprus, disciple of Saint John Lampadistis.
10-11.name: Jonas of Pergamos

10-12.bio:
Saints Probus and Tarachos, together with Andronicus, were Christians of Cilicia who suffered during the persecution under Diocletian at the beginning of the fourth century. Differing in age and station, they were united in their confession; brought repeatedly before the judges, they endured prolonged tortures with astonishing endurance and were finally put to death for Christ.

The faithful reverently gathered their relics, and the three are honored together as steadfast athletes of the faith. They are commemorated on October 12.
10-12.desc: Holy Martyrs Probus, Tarachos, and Andronicus.
10-12.name: Probus and Tarachos

10-12.bio:
Symeon was born in Paphlagonia around 949 and raised in Constantinople, where as a young man he became the disciple of Symeon the Pious of the Studion. He was made abbot of the monastery of Saint Mamas, which he restored in life and discipline.

His teaching that every Christian may consciously experience the grace of the Holy Spirit as light brought him opposition and exile, but his hymns and discourses earned him the title Theologian, given only to two others. He reposed in 1022.
10-12.desc: Venerable Symeon the New Theologian, abbot of Saint Mamas and mystic of the divine light.
10-12.name: Symeon the New Theologian

10-12.bio:
Domnina was a Christian of Anazarbus who was brought before the governor Lysias during the persecution of Diocletian. She confessed Christ and was scourged, her feet were burned, and she was cast into prison.

There she gave up her soul to God, receiving the crown of martyrdom at the end of the third century.
10-12.desc: Holy Martyr Domnina of Anazarbus in Cilicia.
10-12.name: Domnina of Anazarbus

10-12.bio:
Anastasia was a Roman maiden who lived in a community of virgins and was denounced as a Christian in the persecution of Decius. She endured many torments, refusing to deny Christ.

She was finally beheaded, and a Christian named Cyril, who gave her water in her sufferings, was put to death with her.
10-12.desc: Holy Virgin Martyr Anastasia of Rome, who suffered under Decius.
10-12.name: Anastasia the Virgin

10-12.bio:
Juventinus and Maximus were bodyguards of the emperor Julian the Apostate at Antioch. When Julian ordered that the food and water of the city be sprinkled with blood from idol sacrifices, they openly lamented the profanation.

Denounced to the emperor, they refused to recant and were beheaded in 363. Saint John Chrysostom preached in their honor.
10-12.desc: Holy Martyrs Juventinus and Maximus, soldiers of Antioch under Julian the Apostate.
10-12.name: Juventinus and Maximus

10-12.bio: Jason is commemorated in the Synaxarion as a Bishop of Damascus who shepherded his flock in holiness and reposed in peace. The details of his life are not preserved.
10-12.name: Jason of Damascus

10-12.bio:
On this day the Church of Athens gathers in one commemoration all the saints of the city, from Dionysios the Areopagite, Hierotheos and Damaris of apostolic times to Philothei and the New Martyrs of the Turkish yoke.

The feast was established by the Church of Greece to honor the local saints of the capital together.
10-12.desc: Synaxis of all the Saints who shone forth in Athens.
10-12.name: Synaxis of the Saints of Athens

10-13.bio:
Saints Carpus and Papylus suffered for Christ during the persecutions of the third century in Asia Minor. Carpus, a bishop, and Papylus, a deacon known for his care of the sick, refused to offer pagan sacrifice; with their companions they endured torture with joy and received the crown of martyrdom at Pergamum.

Their witness, preserved in some of the most ancient martyr accounts of the Church, strengthened the faithful of Asia Minor in a time of trial. They are commemorated on October 13.
10-13.name: Carpus and Papylus

10-13.bio:
Chrysi was born to a poor Christian family in the village of Slatena in the region of Meglena in Macedonia. Renowned for her beauty, she was seized by a Turk who tried to force her to accept Islam and become his wife.

She refused steadfastly through months of torture and the pleas of her own family, and was finally hanged from a tree in 1795. Her memory is honored by Greeks and Bulgarians alike.
10-13.desc: Holy New Martyr Chrysi (Zlata) of Meglena, the virgin who suffered under the Turks in 1795.
10-13.name: Chrysi the New Martyr

10-13.bio:
Benjamin was a deacon in Persia in the fifth century who converted many from the worship of fire. Imprisoned for two years, he was released on condition that he cease preaching, but he would not be silent.

Seized again, he was cruelly tortured with reeds thrust under his nails and finally impaled, around the year 424.
10-13.desc: Holy Martyr Benjamin the Deacon, who suffered in Persia for preaching Christ.
10-13.name: Benjamin the Deacon

10-13.bio:
Niketas was a nobleman of Paphlagonia and a kinsman of the empress Irene, who made him a patrician and governor of Sicily; he represented the empress at the Seventh Ecumenical Council. He later became a monk.

Under the iconoclast emperors he was imprisoned and exiled for his defense of the holy icons, and reposed in peace in 836 honored as a confessor.
10-13.desc: Venerable Niketas the Confessor and Patrician, who suffered for the holy icons.
10-13.name: Niketas the Confessor

10-13.bio:
Florentios was a Christian of Thessalonica who zealously preached Christ and turned many from idolatry. Brought before the governor, he confessed his faith boldly.

After torture he was burned to death, receiving the crown of martyrdom.
10-13.desc: Holy Martyr Florentios of Thessalonica, burned for the faith.
10-13.name: Florentios of Thessalonica

10-13.bio:
Jacob was abbot of the monastery of the Dormition at Hamatoura in northern Lebanon in the thirteenth century, where he restored the monastic life. Seized by the Mamluk rulers of Tripoli, he was pressed for a year to accept Islam.

He refused and was beheaded and burned; his relics were discovered at the monastery in 1996 and he was glorified by the Patriarchate of Antioch.
10-13.desc: Holy Monk-Martyr Jacob of Hamatoura in Lebanon, who suffered under the Mamluks.
10-13.name: Jacob of Hamatoura

10-14.bio:
Saints Nazarius, Gervasius, and Protasius, with their companion Celsius, were martyrs of the early Church in Italy, put to death for Christ at Milan in the first age of persecution. The synaxaria relate that Nazarius preached the Gospel with apostolic zeal, and that the young Celsius followed him even unto death.

Their relics were found centuries later in Milan in the days of St. Ambrose, to the great joy of the Church, and their veneration spread through both East and West. They are commemorated on October 14.
10-14.desc: Holy Martyrs Nazarius, Gervase, and Prothasius.
10-14.name: Nazarios, Gervase, Prothase

10-14.bio:
Kosmas was an orphan adopted by the father of Saint John of Damascus and educated with him by a learned monk from Calabria. Both entered the Lavra of Saint Sabbas, where Kosmas composed canons for the great feasts, including those of the Nativity, Theophany and Holy Week.

Around 743 he was made Bishop of Maiuma near Gaza, where he reposed in old age.
10-14.desc: Saint Kosmas the Hymnographer, Bishop of Maiuma, foster brother of Saint John of Damascus.
10-14.name: Kosmas the Melodist

10-14.bio:
Paraskevi was born in the eleventh century at Epivates near Constantinople. Moved by the Gospel command to give to the poor, she left home and lived in asceticism in the Jordan desert for many years.

Returning to her homeland, she reposed in peace; her relics were later carried to Trnovo, Belgrade, Constantinople and finally Iasi, where she is honored as the protectress of Moldavia and beloved throughout the Balkans.
10-14.desc: Venerable Paraskevi the New of Epivates, whose relics rest at Iasi in Romania.
10-14.name: Paraskevi the New of Epivates

10-14.bio:
Silvanos was a soldier who left the army to become a priest at Gaza and was later made a bishop. In the persecution of Diocletian and Maximian he was condemned to labor in the copper mines of Phaeno.

There, in old age, he was beheaded with forty companions around 311, receiving the crown of martyrdom.
10-14.desc: Holy Hieromartyr Silvanos of Gaza, beheaded in the copper mines of Palestine.
10-14.name: Silvanos of Gaza

10-14.bio:
Ignatios was born on Lesbos around 1492, married and served as a priest, and after his wife's death became a monk. He was made Metropolitan of Methymna and founded the monastery of the Leimon and the convent of Myrsiniotissa.

He labored to strengthen the faith of his flock under Ottoman rule and reposed in 1566; his relics are kept at the Leimonos monastery, where many miracles are recorded.
10-14.desc: Saint Ignatios Agallianos, Archbishop of Methymna on Lesbos, wonderworker.
10-14.name: Ignatios Agallianos

10-14.bio:
Nicholas, great-grandson of Yaroslav the Wise and Prince of Lutsk, left his wife, children and principality in 1106 to become a monk of the Kiev Caves, the first Russian prince to do so.

He served humbly in the kitchen and as gatekeeper, planted the monastery garden, and founded a hospital. He reposed in 1143 and is venerated as a wonderworker.
10-14.desc: Venerable Nicholas Sviatosha, Prince of Chernigov, monk of the Kiev Caves.
10-14.name: Nicholas Sviatosha

10-15.bio:
St. Lucian was a priest of Antioch, renowned as a scholar of the Holy Scriptures, who labored over the sacred text and taught many disciples in the school of Antioch. During the persecution at the beginning of the fourth century he was arrested and taken to Nicomedia, where after a bold defense of the faith he died in prison for Christ around the year 312.

He is honored as a hieromartyr and teacher whose love for the Scriptures marked the whole church of Antioch. He is commemorated on October 15.
10-15.name: Lucian of Antioch

10-15.bio:
Born Niketas in Galatia in the ninth century, he left his wife and daughter to become a monk on Mount Olympus in Bithynia, and afterward one of the first great ascetics of Mount Athos, living for a time on a pillar near Thessalonica.

He founded the monastery of Peristerai east of Thessalonica and reposed in 898 on the island of Hiera; his relics were brought to Thessalonica.
10-15.desc: Venerable Euthymios the New, ascetic of Mount Athos and founder of the monastery of Peristerai near Thessalonica.
10-15.name: Euthymios the New of Thessalonica

10-15.bio:
Savinos was chosen Bishop of Catania, but after a short time he withdrew secretly to the wilderness to live in asceticism and prayer.

Tradition relates that he received the gifts of healing and discernment and reposed in peace, being honored among the venerable hierarchs.
10-15.desc: Saint Savinos, Bishop of Catania in Sicily.
10-15.name: Savinos of Catania

10-15.bio:
Barses was Bishop of Edessa in the fourth century and a steadfast defender of the Nicene faith. The Arian emperor Valens banished him first to an island and then to Egypt.

He died in exile around 378, and the Church honors him as a confessor.
10-15.desc: Saint Barses the Confessor, Bishop of Edessa, exiled by the Arians.
10-15.name: Barses of Edessa

10-15.bio:
Lucian was a hieromonk of the Kiev Caves Lavra who was martyred during the invasion of Batu Khan around 1243.

His relics rest in the Far Caves of Saint Theodosios, and he is commemorated with the fathers of the Kiev Caves.
10-15.desc: Holy Hieromartyr Lucian the Presbyter of the Kiev Caves, slain in the Tatar invasion.
10-15.name: Lucian of the Kiev Caves

10-15.bio:
Dionysios, born near Kiev, founded the Ascension Caves monastery at Nizhny Novgorod and was made Bishop of Suzdal in 1374. He was a friend of Saint Sergius of Radonezh and a zealous opponent of the Strigolnik heresy.

Consecrated Metropolitan of Kiev in Constantinople in 1384, he was detained in Kiev by the prince and reposed there in 1385.
10-15.desc: Saint Dionysios, Archbishop of Suzdal, founder of the Caves monastery of Nizhny Novgorod.
10-15.name: Dionysios of Suzdal

10-16.bio:
St. Longinus was the centurion who stood guard at the Cross of Christ and, beholding the darkness and the earthquake, confessed: truly this was the Son of God. Tradition holds that he was also among the guards at the tomb, and that having become a believer he left the army and preached Christ in his native Cappadocia.

For this confession he was beheaded, sealing with his blood the faith he first proclaimed on Golgotha. He is commemorated on October 16.
10-16.desc: Holy Martyr Longinus the Centurion who pierced Christ's side.
10-16.name: Longinus the Centurion

10-16.bio:
These four martyrs are commemorated together in the Synaxarion of this day. Tradition relates that they confessed Christ before the pagan authorities and were beheaded.

The details of their lives are not preserved.
10-16.desc: Holy Martyrs Leontios, Dometios, Terentios and Domninos.
10-16.name: Leontios, Dometios, Terentios and Domninos

10-16.bio:
Malos lived as a hermit in the wilderness, where he attained such purity of life that, tradition relates, he was given the grace of working miracles.

He reposed in peace and is honored among the venerable fathers.
10-16.name: Malos the Hermit

10-16.bio:
John was born in the village of Tourkolekas in Messenia in the early nineteenth century, into a family of klephts of the Peloponnese. Taken captive by the Turks as a boy with his father, he was pressed to deny Christ and accept Islam.

Tradition relates that he refused steadfastly and was killed in 1816. He was numbered among the saints by the Church of Greece in recent years.
10-16.desc: Holy New Martyr John of Tourkolekas in Messenia, put to death by the Turks as a boy.
10-16.name: John of Tourkolekas

10-16.bio:
Longinus served for many years as gatekeeper of the Kiev Caves Lavra, fulfilling his humble obedience with unceasing prayer. Tradition relates that he received the gift of discernment, knowing the thoughts of those who entered and left the monastery.

He reposed in the thirteenth or fourteenth century and his relics rest in the Far Caves.
10-16.desc: Venerable Longinus the Gatekeeper of the Kiev Caves.
10-16.name: Longinus the Gatekeeper

10-16.bio:
Gallus was an Irish monk and companion of Saint Columbanus who preached among the pagans of the Lake Constance region. Remaining behind when Columbanus went to Italy, he lived as a hermit in the forest near the river Steinach.

He reposed around 640, and the great abbey of Saint Gall grew up on the site of his cell.
10-16.desc: Venerable Gallus, Irish missionary and hermit, enlightener of the Swiss.
10-16.name: Gallus of Switzerland

10-17.bio:
The holy Prophet Hosea was one of the twelve minor prophets, who prophesied in the northern kingdom of Israel in the eighth century before Christ. Through the image of his own sorrowful marriage he proclaimed the unfailing love of God for His unfaithful people, calling Israel to repentance with words of both judgment and tenderness.

His prophecy, I desire mercy and not sacrifice, was taken up by the Lord Himself in the Gospels. He is commemorated on October 17.
10-17.name: Osee the Prophet

10-17.bio:
Andrew was a monk of Crete who, hearing of the iconoclast persecution of Constantine Copronymus, went to Constantinople and rebuked the emperor to his face in the church of Saint Mamas.

He was scourged and dragged through the streets, and died from his wounds around 767; his body was cast into a pit at the place called Krisis, whence his name.
10-17.desc: Holy Monk-Martyr Andrew of Crete, slain in Constantinople for the holy icons.
10-17.name: Andrew of Crete the Monk-Martyr

10-17.bio: These Kosmas and Damianos, distinct from the Unmercenaries of Asia and of Rome, were physicians of Arabia who healed freely in the name of Christ. They were seized at Aegae in Cilicia in the persecution of Diocletian and, when torments failed to harm them, were beheaded with their three brothers around 287.
10-17.desc: Holy Unmercenaries Kosmas and Damianos of Arabia and their brothers Leontios, Anthimos and Euprepios, martyred in Cilicia.
10-17.greek: Κοσμάς, Δαμιανός, Λεόντιος, Άνθιμος και Ευπρέπιος
10-17.name: Kosmas and Damianos of Arabia

10-17.bio:
After the Lord raised him from the dead, Lazarus fled the hatred of the Jews and came to Cyprus, where he was made Bishop of Kition and served for many years before his second death.

In 890 the emperor Leo the Wise had his relics translated from Kition to Constantinople and built a church in his honor; the Church commemorates the event on this day.
10-17.desc: Translation of the relics of Saint Lazarus, friend of Christ and Bishop of Kition, to Constantinople.
10-17.name: Lazarus the Four-Days-Dead (Translation of Relics)

10-17.bio: Isidora and Neophyte are commemorated together in the Synaxarion of this day among the holy women who pleased God. The details of their lives are not preserved, and tradition relates only that they reposed in peace.
10-17.name: Isidora and Neophyte

10-17.bio: These five martyrs are commemorated together in the Synaxarion of this day. Tradition relates that they confessed Christ and were put to death for the faith; the details of their sufferings are not preserved.
10-17.desc: Holy Martyrs Antigonos, Loukianos, Terentios, Nikomedes and Theophanes.
10-17.greek: Αντίγονος, Λουκιανός, Τερέντιος, Νικομήδης και Θεοφάνης
10-17.name: Antigonos, Loukianos, Terentios, Nikomedes and Theophanes

10-18.bio:
St. Luke the Evangelist was a physician of Antioch and a companion of the Apostle Paul in his missionary labors. He wrote the third Gospel, which preserves the fullest account of the Nativity and the parables of divine mercy, and the Acts of the Apostles, the history of the Church's first years.

Tradition honors him also as the first iconographer, who painted the image of the Most Holy Theotokos, and relates that he served the Gospel into old age in Greece. The beloved physician and evangelist is commemorated on October 18.
10-18.name: Luke the Evangelist

10-18.bio:
Marinos was an old man of Anazarbus who confessed Christ before the governor Lysias in the persecution of Diocletian. Despite his age he endured beatings and tortures.

He was finally beheaded, receiving the crown of martyrdom at the end of the third century.
10-18.desc: Holy Martyr Marinos the Elder of Anazarbus in Cilicia.
10-18.name: Marinos the Elder

10-18.bio:
Julian lived in a cave near the Euphrates in the fourth century, eating only once a week and spending his days in prayer. Many disciples gathered around him.

Tradition relates that while praying for the Church he learned of the death of the emperor Julian the Apostate at the very hour it happened; he reposed in peace around 370.
10-18.desc: Venerable Julian the Hermit of Mesopotamia, who foretold the death of Julian the Apostate.
10-18.name: Julian the Hermit of the Euphrates

10-18.bio:
Gabriel and Kyrmidoles were Christians of Egypt who were falsely accused before the Muslim authorities of Cairo and pressed to accept Islam.

Refusing to deny Christ, they were beheaded in 1522 and are honored among the New Martyrs.
10-18.desc: Holy New Martyrs Gabriel and Kyrmidoles, who suffered in Egypt in 1522.
10-18.name: Gabriel and Kyrmidoles

10-18.bio:
The brothers Symeon and Theodore, monks from Thessalonica, were guided by a vision to a great cave in the mountains of Achaia. There, tradition relates, the shepherdess Euphrosyne led them to an icon of the Theotokos painted by the Evangelist Luke, hidden in the cave.

They founded on that spot the monastery of Mega Spilaion, one of the oldest in Greece, and reposed in peace.
10-18.desc: Venerable Symeon and Theodore, founders of the Monastery of Mega Spilaion, and the shepherdess Euphrosyne.
10-18.name: Symeon and Theodore of Mega Spilaion

10-18.bio:
Mnason of Cyprus is mentioned in the Acts of the Apostles as an early disciple who gave hospitality to Saint Paul in Jerusalem. Tradition relates that he was made Bishop of Tamassos by Saint Herakleidios.

He shepherded the Christians of Cyprus in apostolic times and reposed in peace.
10-18.desc: Saint Mnason, Bishop of Tamassos in Cyprus, the early disciple named in the Acts of the Apostles.
10-18.name: Mnason of Cyprus

10-19.bio:
The holy Prophet Joel was one of the twelve minor prophets, who prophesied in the kingdom of Judah. In a time of devastation he called the people to fasting and heartfelt repentance, and he foretold the day when God would pour out His Spirit upon all flesh.

That prophecy was fulfilled at Pentecost, when the Apostle Peter proclaimed Joel's words to the crowds in Jerusalem at the descent of the Holy Spirit. He is commemorated on October 19.
10-19.name: Joel the Prophet

10-19.bio:
Cleopatra was a widow of Edra near Mount Tabor whose husband had been a Roman officer in Egypt. Witnessing the martyrdom of Saint Varus, she secretly recovered his body and brought it home to Palestine, where she built a church in his honor.

Tradition relates that when her only son John died on the day of the church's consecration, Varus and the boy appeared to her in glory; she lived the rest of her life in prayer beside the church and reposed in peace in the fourth century.
10-19.desc: Blessed Cleopatra of Palestine, who honored the relics of the Martyr Varus.
10-19.name: Cleopatra the Righteous

10-19.bio:
Varus was a Roman officer in Egypt and a secret Christian who visited and cared for imprisoned confessors. When one of seven imprisoned monks died before trial, Varus took his place, declaring himself a Christian.

He was tortured and beheaded with the others around 307, and his relics were taken to Palestine by the blessed Cleopatra.
10-19.desc: Holy Martyr Varus and the six monk-martyrs of Egypt who suffered with him.
10-19.name: Varus and the Six Monk-Martyrs

10-19.bio:
Sadoth succeeded Saint Symeon as Bishop of Seleucia-Ctesiphon in Persia during the persecution of King Shapur II. Arrested with his clergy and many of the faithful, he refused to worship the sun.

After months of imprisonment and torture he was beheaded with one hundred and twenty-eight companions around 342.
10-19.desc: Holy Hieromartyr Sadoth, Bishop of Persia, and the one hundred and twenty-eight martyrs with him.
10-19.name: Sadoth of Persia

10-19.bio:
John was born in the village of Skrino near Sofia in the ninth century and became a monk while young. He lived for years in a hollow tree and then in a cave in the Rila mountains, in fasting and prayer, until disciples gathered and the great Rila monastery was founded.

He reposed in 946; this day commemorates the translation of his relics from Sredets to Trnovo in 1238.
10-19.desc: Venerable John of Rila, wonderworker and patron of the Bulgarian people.
10-19.name: John of Rila

10-19.bio: Leontios is commemorated in the Synaxarion as a philosopher who forsook worldly wisdom for the ascetic life and reposed in peace. The details of his life are not preserved.
10-19.name: Leontios the Philosopher

10-2.bio:
St. Cyprian was a famed sorcerer of Antioch who was hired to bend the Christian virgin Justina to an unwanted suitor. Every art of his magic was shattered against her prayer and the sign of the Cross, and Cyprian, recognizing a power greater than all his demons, burned his books, was baptized, and in time became a bishop of the Church.

During the persecution under Diocletian, Cyprian and Justina were arrested, tortured, and beheaded together. They are invoked by the faithful against the works of magic and are commemorated on October 2.
10-2.name: Cyprian and Justina

10-2.bio:
Theophilos entered monastic life as a youth under the elder Stephen on Mount Selenteia and grew in obedience and prayer. During the iconoclast persecution of Leo the Isaurian he boldly defended the veneration of the holy icons.

For this he was flogged and sent into exile, where he died in peace after long sufferings, and so is honored as a confessor.
10-2.desc: Venerable Theophilos the Confessor, monk of Bulgaria who suffered for the holy icons.
10-2.name: Theophilos the Confessor

10-2.bio:
George was a Christian of Asia Minor who was falsely accused by the Turks and pressed to accept Islam. Refusing to deny Christ, he endured beatings and imprisonment.

He was put to death at Karatzasou, and the Church honors him among the New Martyrs of the Turkish yoke.
10-2.desc: Holy New Martyr George, who suffered at Karatzasou in Asia Minor under the Ottomans.
10-2.name: George the New Martyr of Karatzasou

10-2.bio:
Theodore Gavras was a Byzantine nobleman and governor of Trebizond in the late eleventh century, famed for defending the Pontic lands against the Seljuk Turks. Captured in battle, he was urged to accept Islam with promises of honor.

He refused, and after torture was beheaded around 1098. The people of Pontus have honored him ever since as their protector and great martyr.
10-2.desc: Holy Great Martyr Theodore Gavras, governor of Trebizond, beheaded by the Turks for refusing to deny Christ.
10-2.name: Theodore Gavras the Great Martyr

10-2.bio:
Born Constantine, of a princely family of Mangup in the Crimea, he came to Moscow in 1478 in the retinue of the Byzantine princess Sophia Palaiologina. Renouncing the world, he was tonsured at the Ferapontov monastery with the name Cassian.

He later founded a monastery near Uglich, where he lived in strict asceticism and reposed at the end of the fifteenth century, being venerated as a wonderworker.
10-2.desc: Venerable Cassian the Greek, wonderworker of Uglich, a Byzantine prince who became a monk in Russia.
10-2.name: Cassian the Greek of Uglich

10-2.bio:
Theodore Ushakov, born in 1745, commanded the Russian Black Sea fleet and never lost a battle or a ship. In 1798 to 1799 he freed the Ionian Islands from the French and helped establish self-government there, for which the Greeks of Corfu and Cephalonia held him in deep gratitude.

In retirement he lived near the Sanaksar monastery in prayer and almsgiving, reposing in 1817. He was glorified by the Russian Church in 2001.
10-2.desc: Righteous Theodore Ushakov, admiral of the Russian fleet and liberator of the Ionian Islands.
10-2.name: Theodore Ushakov the Admiral

10-20.bio:
The holy Great Martyr Artemios was a distinguished military commander of the fourth century who served under St. Constantine the Great and his successors. When the Emperor Julian the Apostate sought to restore paganism, Artemios rebuked him openly for his persecution of the Christians; for this he was stripped of his rank, cruelly tortured, and beheaded at Antioch in the year 362.

His relics were brought to Constantinople, where many miracles of healing were wrought, and he has long been invoked by the faithful for healing of bodily ailments. He is commemorated on October 20.
10-20.name: Artemon of Seleucia

10-20.bio:
Matrona was born Mary in the village of Volissos on Chios to wealthy parents. Refusing marriage, she fled to a small convent near the town of Chios, where she was tonsured and later became abbess, enlarging the community by her own labors.

She was known for her severe asceticism and gift of healing, and reposed in the late fifteenth century; she is one of the most beloved saints of Chios.
10-20.desc: Venerable Matrona of Chios, the wonderworker and abbess of the island.
10-20.name: Matrona of Chios

10-20.bio:
Gerasimos was born at Trikala in Corinthia in 1506 of the noble Notaras family. He became a monk on Mount Athos, lived in the Holy Land and on Zakynthos, and finally settled on Cephalonia, where he founded the convent of New Jerusalem at Omala.

He reposed in 1579; his relics were found incorrupt and are honored on August 16 and on this day of their translation, with many healings, especially of the possessed.
10-20.desc: Translation of the relics of Venerable Gerasimos the New Ascetic, protector of Cephalonia.
10-20.name: Gerasimos of Cephalonia (Translation of Relics)

10-20.bio:
These four Christians of Caesarea in Palestine boldly rebuked the governor Firmilian for sacrificing to idols during the persecution of Maximian.

After torture they were beheaded around 308, and the maiden Manatho was burned with them.
10-20.desc: Holy Martyrs Zebinas, Germanos, Nikephoros and Antoninos of Caesarea in Palestine.
10-20.name: Zebinas, Germanos, Nikephoros and Antoninos

10-20.bio: Manatho was a virgin of Scythopolis in Palestine who confessed Christ before the governor Firmilian at Caesarea. After scourging she was burned to death together with the martyrs Zebinas, Germanos, Nikephoros and Antoninos around 308.
10-20.desc: Holy Virgin Martyr Manatho of Scythopolis, burned at Caesarea.
10-20.name: Manatho the Virgin

10-20.bio: Basil is commemorated in the Synaxarion as a Bishop of Trebizond who shepherded his flock in holiness and reposed in peace. The details of his life are not preserved.
10-20.name: Basil of Trebizond

10-21.bio:
St. Hilarion the Great was born near Gaza in Palestine at the end of the third century. Inspired by the example of St. Anthony the Great, whom he visited in the Egyptian desert, he took up the ascetic life in his homeland and became the father of monasticism in Palestine, drawing many disciples by his fasting, humility, and gift of wonderworking.

Fleeing the fame of his miracles, he wandered from land to land seeking stillness, and reposed in Cyprus in old age. He is commemorated on October 21.
10-21.desc: Venerable Hilarion the Great, father of Palestinian monasticism.
10-21.name: Hilarion the Great

10-21.bio:
Philotheos was born in 1526 at Elateia in Asia Minor and was taken captive with his brother by the Turks as a child; his mother, who had become a nun, later found and freed them. He became a monk at the monastery of Dionysiou on Mount Athos.

He lived for many years in fasting and silence in the wilderness of the Holy Mountain, gathered disciples, and reposed in peace in old age.
10-21.desc: Venerable Philotheos of Dionysiou, ascetic of Mount Athos.
10-21.name: Philotheos of Athos

10-21.bio:
Theodote and the priest Socrates were Christians of Ancyra in Galatia who confessed Christ during the persecution of Alexander Severus in the third century.

Brought before the governor, they refused to sacrifice to idols, were tortured, and were beheaded together around 230.
10-21.desc: Holy Martyrs Theodote and Socrates the Presbyter of Ancyra.
10-21.name: Theodote and Socrates

10-21.bio:
John was born in 1758 in a village near Monemvasia, the son of a priest. In 1770 Albanian raiders killed his father and carried the boy and his mother into slavery in Larissa, where his Turkish master tried by every means to make him accept Islam.

He refused steadfastly for three years, and in 1773, at the age of fifteen, he was stabbed by his master and died confessing Christ.
10-21.desc: Holy New Martyr John of Monemvasia, who died for Christ in Larissa in 1773.
10-21.name: John of Monemvasia

10-21.bio:
Christodoulos was born in Bithynia in the eleventh century and lived as a monk in Palestine, on Mount Latros and on Kos before receiving the island of Patmos from the emperor Alexios Komnenos in 1088. There he founded the monastery of Saint John the Theologian.

He died on Euboea in 1093 after fleeing pirate raids; his relics were returned to Patmos, and the Church commemorates their translation on this day.
10-21.desc: Translation of the relics of Venerable Christodoulos, founder of the Monastery of Saint John on Patmos.
10-21.name: Christodoulos of Patmos (Translation of Relics)

10-21.bio:
Gaius, Dasius and Zotikos were Christians of Nicomedia who in the persecution of Diocletian destroyed a pagan temple. Seized and tortured, they refused to deny Christ.

They were bound with stones and drowned in the sea around 303, receiving the crown of martyrdom.
10-21.desc: Holy Martyrs Gaius, Dasius and Zotikos, drowned at Nicomedia.
10-21.name: Gaius, Dasius and Zotikos

10-21.bio: Ursula was, according to tradition, a British princess who with a company of virgins was martyred by the Huns at Cologne while returning from a pilgrimage to Rome. The Church honors her among the virgin martyrs of the West before the schism.
10-21.desc: Holy Virgin Martyr Ursula of Cologne and her companions.
10-21.name: Ursula the Virgin

10-22.bio:
St. Abercius was Bishop of Hierapolis in Phrygia in the second century, called Equal-to-the-Apostles for his missionary zeal. He overthrew the idols of his city, brought multitudes to faith in Christ by his preaching and healings, and journeyed as far as Rome and the lands of the East, everywhere confirming the churches.

His famous epitaph, composed by the saint himself, speaks in veiled language of the Eucharist and the universal Church, and stands among the most precious monuments of early Christianity. He is commemorated on October 22.
10-22.name: Abercius of Hieropolis

10-22.bio:
Alexander was a bishop in the region of Adrianople who converted many pagans by his preaching. Brought before the governor, he refused to sacrifice to idols and was tortured.

The soldier Herakleios and the women Anna, Elizabeth, Theodote and Glykeria, moved by his endurance, confessed Christ and were beheaded with him around the third century.
10-22.desc: Holy Hieromartyr Alexander, Bishop of Adrianople, and the martyrs Herakleios, Anna, Elizabeth, Theodote and Glykeria with him.
10-22.name: Alexander of Adrianople

10-22.bio:
Abba Lot was a Desert Father of Egypt in the fifth century whose sayings are preserved in the Paradise of the Fathers. Best known is his exchange with Abba Joseph, who told him that if he wished, he could become all flame.

He reposed in peace and is honored among the venerable fathers.
10-22.desc: Venerable Abba Lot of Egypt, one of the Desert Fathers.
10-22.name: Lot of Egypt

10-22.bio: Rufus is commemorated in the Synaxarion as an ascetic who lived in the wilderness and reposed in peace. The details of his life are not preserved.
10-22.name: Rufus the Venerable

10-22.bio:
Gregory was Bishop of Methone in the Peloponnese at the outbreak of the Greek Revolution of 1821 and blessed the struggle of his people. Tradition relates that he was seized by the forces of Ibrahim Pasha and killed for his faith and nation.

He is honored among the ethno-hieromartyrs of the Church of Greece.
10-22.desc: Holy Ethno-Hieromartyr Gregory, Bishop of Methone, who suffered in the Greek War of Independence.
10-22.name: Gregory of Methone

10-22.bio: Zacharias is commemorated in the Synaxarion of this day among the martyrs who confessed Christ unto death. The details of his sufferings are not preserved.
10-22.name: Zacharias the Martyr

10-23.bio:
St. Ignatius was Patriarch of Constantinople in the ninth century. The son of an emperor, he was tonsured a monk in his youth after his father's fall from power, and rose by his virtue to the patriarchal throne, which he occupied twice amid the turbulence of imperial politics, suffering deposition and exile for his firmness.

He bore his trials with patience and forgiveness, and ended his days in peace, honored for his ascetic life and his steadfastness as a shepherd of the Church. He is commemorated on October 23.
10-23.name: Ignatius, Patriarch of Constantinople

10-23.bio:
James was the son of Joseph the Betrothed and is called the Brother of the Lord. He was chosen by the apostles as the first Bishop of Jerusalem, presided at the Apostolic Council, and composed the Epistle that bears his name and the earliest form of the Divine Liturgy.

Called the Just even by the Jews for his ascetic life, he was thrown from the pinnacle of the Temple and clubbed to death around the year 62 for confessing Christ.
10-23.desc: Holy Apostle James the Brother of the Lord, first Bishop of Jerusalem.
10-23.name: James the Brother of the Lord

10-23.bio:
Makarios, according to the account of three monks who found him, was a Roman who fled from his wedding feast to seek God and was led by an angel to a cave in the far wilderness of Mesopotamia.

There he lived in extreme asceticism for many years, guarded by two lions, and gave the wandering monks spiritual counsel before sending them home.
10-23.desc: Venerable Makarios the Roman, hermit of Mesopotamia.
10-23.name: Makarios the Roman

10-23.bio: Petronios was a disciple of Saint Pachomios the Great in Egypt and was appointed by him to lead the community after his death. Tradition relates that he reposed in peace only a short time after his teacher, in the fourth century.
10-23.desc: Venerable Petronios, disciple of Saint Pachomios.
10-23.name: Petronios the Venerable

10-23.bio: Nikephoros is commemorated in the Synaxarion as a venerable father who lived in asceticism and reposed in peace. The details of his life are not preserved.
10-23.name: Nikephoros the Venerable

10-23.bio: The Synaxarion of this day commemorates two children who confessed Christ and were put to death for the faith. Their names are not preserved.
10-23.desc: Two holy child martyrs who suffered for Christ.
10-23.name: Two Children Martyrs

10-24.bio:
St. Arethas was the chief of the Christians of Najran in southern Arabia in the sixth century. When a persecutor seized the city and demanded that its people renounce Christ, the aged Arethas strengthened his fellow Christians in the faith, and with a great multitude of men, women, and children he was put to death around the year 523.

The blood of the martyrs of Najran bore witness to Christ in the Arabian peninsula, and their memory was honored throughout the Christian East. St. Arethas and those with him are commemorated on October 24.
10-24.name: Arethas of Najran

10-24.bio:
Sebastiane, according to tradition a disciple of the Apostle Paul, was brought before the governor Sergius at Marcianopolis in the reign of Domitian. She was cast into a furnace and thrown to wild beasts but was preserved unharmed.

She was finally beheaded at Heraclea in Thrace, and the Church honors her among the earliest women martyrs.
10-24.desc: Holy Martyr Sebastiane of Heraclea, disciple of the Apostle Paul.
10-24.name: Sebastiane the Martyr

10-24.bio:
Mark, Soterichos and Valentine were Christians of Asia Minor who were arrested during the persecution of Diocletian. After torture they were tied to horses and dragged over rocks until they died.

Their relics were later carried to the island of Thasos, where they were honored with a church.
10-24.desc: Holy Martyrs Mark, Soterichos and Valentine of Asia.
10-24.name: Mark, Soterichos and Valentine

10-24.bio: Akakios was a priest who confessed Christ before the pagan authorities and was tortured for the faith. Tradition relates that he was beheaded, receiving the crown of martyrdom.
10-24.name: Akakios the Presbyter

10-24.bio:
Among the Christians of Najran who suffered under the Jewish king Dhu Nuwas was a woman whose small child, tradition relates, cried out that he too was a Christian and asked to die with his mother.

Both were cast into the fire together with the martyrs of Arethas around 523.
10-24.desc: The holy woman and her infant martyred at Najran with Saint Arethas.
10-24.name: The Holy Woman and her Infant

10-24.bio:
Arethas was a monk of the Kiev Caves who secretly hoarded wealth in his cell. When thieves stole it, he raged and blamed the innocent, until in a vision during illness he saw angels and demons contending for his soul.

Repenting, he thanked God for the loss and thereafter lived as a recluse in thanksgiving and prayer, reposing in the twelfth century.
10-24.desc: Venerable Arethas the Recluse of the Kiev Caves.
10-24.name: Arethas of the Kiev Caves

10-25.bio:
St. Tabitha, called Dorcas in Greek, was a disciple of Christ living at Joppa in the days of the apostles. The Acts of the Apostles describes her as full of good works and almsgiving, sewing garments for the widows and the poor; when she fell sick and died, the Apostle Peter was summoned, and by his prayer God raised her from the dead.

Her restoration to life brought many in Joppa to believe in the Lord, and she remains a model of practical, quiet charity. She is commemorated on October 25.
10-25.name: Tabitha

10-25.bio:
Markianos, a reader, and Martyrios, a subdeacon, served as secretaries to Saint Paul the Confessor, Patriarch of Constantinople, and defended the Orthodox faith against the Arians.

When bribes and threats failed to win them over, they were beheaded around 355; Saint John Chrysostom later built a church over their tomb.
10-25.desc: Holy Martyrs Markianos and Martyrios, notaries of Constantinople, slain by the Arians.
10-25.name: Markianos and Martyrios the Notaries

10-25.bio:
Anastasios was a cloth-fuller from Aquileia who settled at Salona in Dalmatia and painted a cross over the door of his workshop. Denounced as a Christian in the persecution of Diocletian, he confessed Christ boldly.

He was drowned in the sea with a stone around his neck, and his body was recovered by a pious woman and buried with honor.
10-25.desc: Holy Martyr Anastasios the Fuller of Salona in Dalmatia.
10-25.name: Anastasios the Fuller

10-25.bio:
George was born at Kromna near Amastris in Paphlagonia and lived as a hermit on Mount Agrioserika before the people of Amastris chose him as their bishop. He was consecrated in Constantinople and shepherded his flock with great wisdom.

He defended the city from Arab attack by his prayers and reposed around 805; tradition relates that his intercession later saved Amastris from a raid of the Rus.
10-25.desc: Saint George, Bishop of Amastris in Paphlagonia, wonderworker.
10-25.name: George of Amastris

10-25.bio: Makarios is commemorated in the Synaxarion as a Bishop of Paphos in Cyprus who shepherded his flock in holiness and reposed in peace. The details of his life are not preserved.
10-25.desc: Venerable Makarios, Bishop of Paphos in Cyprus.
10-25.name: Makarios of Paphos

10-25.bio: Chrysanthe is commemorated in the Synaxarion of this day among the women martyrs who confessed Christ unto death. The details of her sufferings are not preserved.
10-25.name: Chrysanthe the Martyr

10-26.bio:
St. Demetrios the Great Martyr and Myrrh-Streamer was a young nobleman and military commander of Thessaloniki, martyred under the Emperor Maximian at the beginning of the fourth century. Imprisoned for openly teaching the faith, he blessed the young Nestor, who defeated the gladiator Lyaios in the arena; for this Demetrios was run through with spears in his prison.

From his relics, according to tradition, fragrant myrrh flowed, and he is honored as the great protector of Thessaloniki, where his basilica has stood for fifteen centuries. His feast on October 26 is one of the great celebrations of northern Greece.
10-26.desc: Great Martyr Demetrios of Thessaloniki, Myrrh-Streamer.
10-26.name: Demetrios the Great Martyr

10-26.bio:
On October 26, 740, in the reign of the iconoclast emperor Leo the Isaurian, a great earthquake struck Constantinople, destroying walls and churches. The people understood it as a call to repentance and turned to the Theotokos and Saint Demetrios, whose feast it was.

The Church has since kept the memory of this deliverance together with the feast of the Great Martyr.
10-26.desc: Commemoration of the great earthquake at Constantinople in 740, from which the city was delivered by the prayers of the Theotokos and Saint Demetrios.
10-26.name: Commemoration of the Great Earthquake

10-26.bio:
Loupos was the faithful servant of Saint Demetrios who stood by his master at his martyrdom, gathered his blood-stained garment and ring, and worked healings with them among the people of Thessalonica.

When this became known to the emperor Maximian, Loupos was beheaded, sharing his master's crown.
10-26.desc: Holy Martyr Loupos, servant of Saint Demetrios of Thessalonica.
10-26.name: Loupos the Martyr

10-26.bio:
Joasaph was a monk and iconographer of the monastery of Dionysiou on Mount Athos, tonsured by the abbot Stephen. Longing for martyrdom, he went to Constantinople with the abbot's blessing.

There he confessed Christ before the Turkish authorities and was beheaded in 1536, receiving the crown of martyrdom.
10-26.desc: Holy New Monk-Martyr Joasaph of Dionysiou Monastery on Mount Athos, who suffered at Constantinople in 1536.
10-26.name: Joasaph of Dionysiou

10-26.bio: Artemidoros and Basil are commemorated together in the Synaxarion of this day. Tradition relates that they confessed Christ and were beheaded; the details of their lives are not preserved.
10-26.name: Artemidoros and Basil

10-26.bio:
George, a poor groom from the village of Tzourchli in Epirus, was hanged at Ioannina in 1838 for refusing to deny Christ after a false accusation that he had once become a Muslim. His relics were found incorrupt and became a source of many miracles.

The Church commemorates their solemn translation on this day, alongside his feast on January 17.
10-26.desc: Translation of the relics of the Holy New Martyr George of Ioannina.
10-26.name: George of Ioannina (Translation of Relics)

10-27.bio:
St. Nestor was a young Christian of Thessaloniki, a disciple of the Great Martyr Demetrios. When the gladiator Lyaios was slaying challengers to the delight of the Emperor Maximian, Nestor received the blessing of the imprisoned Demetrios, entered the arena with the prayer, God of Demetrios, help me, and overthrew the boastful champion.

For this the enraged emperor ordered Nestor put to death, and he received the crown of martyrdom the day after his teacher. He is commemorated on October 27, in the afterglow of the feast of St. Demetrios.
10-27.name: Nestor the Martyr

10-27.bio:
The Gospel of Matthew records that Pilate's wife sent word to him during the trial of Christ, saying she had suffered much in a dream because of that righteous man and urging him to have nothing to do with Him.

Tradition names her Prokla or Claudia Procula and relates that she later became a Christian; the Church honors her for her witness at the Passion.
10-27.desc: Saint Prokla, the wife of Pontius Pilate, who pleaded for the Righteous One.
10-27.name: Prokla the Wife of Pilate

10-27.bio:
Capitolina was a wealthy noblewoman of Cappadocia who freed her slaves and gave her goods to the poor before presenting herself to the governor as a Christian. She was beheaded around 304.

Her maid Erotheis, seeing this, threw stones at the governor, confessed Christ, and was beheaded the following day.
10-27.desc: Holy Martyrs Capitolina and her servant Erotheis of Cappadocia.
10-27.name: Capitolina and Erotheis

10-27.bio:
Kyriakos was steward of the Great Church of Constantinople and was elected Patriarch in 595, succeeding Saint John the Faster. He governed the Church in the reigns of Maurice and Phocas and built a church of the Theotokos in the Diakonissa quarter.

He reposed in peace in 606.
10-27.name: Kyriakos of Constantinople

10-27.bio:
Demetrios was a shepherd of the village of Basarabov on the river Lom in Bulgaria in the thirteenth century who became a monk and then a hermit in a cave near the village, living in prayer and great humility.

His relics were found incorrupt and worked many miracles; in 1774 they were brought to Bucharest, where he is honored as protector of the city.
10-27.desc: Venerable Demetrios the New of Basarabov, patron of Bucharest.
10-27.name: Demetrios the New of Basarabov

10-27.bio:
Nestor entered the Kiev Caves monastery in his youth under Saint Theodosios and was ordained hierodeacon. He wrote the lives of Saints Boris and Gleb and of Saint Theodosios, and is honored as the author of the Tale of Bygone Years, the earliest chronicle of the Rus.

He reposed around 1114, and his relics rest in the Near Caves.
10-27.desc: Venerable Nestor the Chronicler of the Kiev Caves, author of the Primary Chronicle.
10-27.name: Nestor the Chronicler

10-28.bio:
St. Terentios suffered for Christ in the early centuries of persecution together with his wife Neonilla and their children. Refusing to deny the faith in which they had raised their household, the whole family confessed Christ together and together received the crown of martyrdom.

They are honored as an image of the Christian family united in faith even unto death, parents and children strengthening one another in their confession. They are commemorated on October 28.
10-28.name: Terentios and companions

10-28.bio:
The Church of Greece in 1952 transferred the feast of the Protection of the Theotokos from October 1 to October 28, joining it to the national anniversary of the refusal of the Italian ultimatum in 1940, in thanksgiving for the protection of the Mother of God during the war.

The feast recalls the vision of Saint Andrew the Fool at Blachernae, who saw the Theotokos spreading her veil over the praying people.
10-28.desc: Feast of the Holy Protection of the Theotokos as kept in Greece on the anniversary of the OXI of 1940.
10-28.name: Protection of the Theotokos (Greek Observance)

10-28.bio:
Stephen was a nephew of Saint John of Damascus and entered the Lavra of Saint Sabbas as a boy, where he was raised by his uncle. He became renowned for his asceticism, his gift of discernment, and the canons and hymns he composed.

He reposed in peace in the late eighth century.
10-28.desc: Venerable Stephen the Sabbaite, hymnographer of the Lavra of Saint Sabbas.
10-28.name: Stephen the Sabbaite

10-28.bio:
Born Alexios in Adrianople around 1230, he became a monk on Mount Athos and in Palestine and lived in great austerity on Mount Ganos. He was made Patriarch of Constantinople in 1289 and again in 1303.

He labored to reform the clergy and feed the poor during the famine and Turkish incursions of his day, and reposed around 1310; his relics were found incorrupt.
10-28.desc: Saint Athanasios I, Patriarch of Constantinople, ascetic and reformer.
10-28.name: Athanasios I of Constantinople

10-28.bio:
Judas, a Jew of Jerusalem, revealed to the empress Helen the place where the Cross of Christ lay hidden. Coming to faith, he was baptized with the name Kyriakos and later became Bishop of Jerusalem.

Tradition relates that under Julian the Apostate he was tortured and martyred together with his mother Anna.
10-28.desc: Holy Hieromartyr Kyriakos, Patriarch of Jerusalem, who showed Saint Helen the place of the Cross, and his mother Anna.
10-28.name: Kyriakos of Jerusalem

10-28.bio:
Angelis, Manuel, George and Nicholas were Christians of the village of Melambes in Crete who had been forced to profess Islam outwardly. In 1824, during the Cretan uprising, they openly returned to the faith of Christ.

Seized by the Turks, they refused to deny Him and were beheaded at Rethymno, receiving the crown of martyrdom.
10-28.desc: Holy New Martyrs Angelis, Manuel, George and Nicholas of Melambes in Crete, beheaded at Rethymno in 1824.
10-28.name: New Martyrs of Melambes

10-28.bio:
Arsenios was a monk of Zica under Saint Sava, who made him abbot and, on leaving for the Holy Land, appointed him his successor as Archbishop of Serbia in 1233.

He governed the Serbian Church for thirty years, moved the see to Pec, and reposed in 1266; his relics were found incorrupt.
10-28.desc: Saint Arsenios, Archbishop of Serbia, successor of Saint Sava.
10-28.name: Arsenios of Serbia

10-29.bio:
St. Anastasios is remembered as a hierarch who served the Church of Constantinople, of whom the synaxaria preserve little beyond his faithful service and holy repose.

The Church honors in him, as in many shepherds whose deeds are known fully to God alone, the quiet faithfulness of those who kept the flock of Christ in difficult times. He is commemorated on October 29.
10-29.name: Anastasios the Younger

10-29.bio:
Anastasia was orphaned at the age of three and raised in a convent near Rome by the abbess Sophia. At twenty, during the persecution of Decius, she was denounced as a Christian and brought before the governor Probus.

Refusing to sacrifice or to marry, she was stretched on the rack, her breasts and tongue were cut off, and she was finally beheaded around 250.
10-29.desc: Holy Monk-Martyr Anastasia the Roman, the virgin who suffered under Decius.
10-29.name: Anastasia the Roman

10-29.bio:
Abramios fled his wedding to become a hermit near Edessa, and was later sent by the bishop to convert a pagan village, which he won by his patience. His orphaned niece Mary lived beside him in asceticism from childhood.

When Mary fell into sin and fled to a life of shame, Abramios sought her out disguised as a soldier and brought her back to repentance; both reposed in peace in the fourth century, and Saint Ephraim wrote their life.
10-29.desc: Venerable Abramios the Recluse of Edessa and his niece Mary.
10-29.name: Abramios the Recluse and Mary

10-29.bio:
Melitine was a Christian of Marcianopolis in Thrace in the reign of Antoninus. Brought to the temple, she overthrew the idols by her prayer and converted many, including the wife of the governor.

She was beheaded, and her body was carried by a Christian toward Lemnos, where she is honored.
10-29.desc: Holy Martyr Melitine of Marcianopolis in Thrace.
10-29.name: Melitine the Martyr

10-29.bio:
Anna was a noblewoman of Constantinople in the ninth century who, widowed, gave her goods to the poor and, disguised as a man, entered a monastery on Mount Olympus in Bithynia with the name Euphemianos.

She was recognized only late in life and reposed in peace, honored among the venerable women who hid their sex for the sake of asceticism.
10-29.desc: Venerable Anna of Constantinople, who lived as the monk Euphemianos.
10-29.name: Anna renamed Euphemianos

10-29.bio:
Timothy, born Triantaphyllos in Thrace, had once accepted Islam under pressure with his wife. Repenting, he went to Mount Athos and became a monk at Esphigmenou, and after preparation by prayer and fasting he returned to Adrianople to confess Christ publicly.

He was beheaded there in 1820, receiving the crown of martyrdom.
10-29.desc: Holy New Monk-Martyr Timothy of Esphigmenou Monastery, beheaded at Adrianople in 1820.
10-29.name: Timothy of Esphigmenou

10-29.bio:
Athanasios was a priest from Sparta in the region of Attaleia in Asia Minor who was falsely accused by the Turks and pressed to accept Islam.

He refused to deny Christ and was beheaded at Mudania in 1653, and is honored among the New Hieromartyrs.
10-29.desc: Holy Hieromartyr Athanasios of Sparta in Attaleia, beheaded at Mudania in 1653.
10-29.name: Athanasios of Sparta in Attaleia

10-3.bio:
St. Dionysios the Areopagite was an Athenian of the first century, a member of the court of the Areopagus, converted when the Apostle Paul preached in Athens of the God whom the city honored without knowing. According to tradition he became the first Bishop of Athens and ended his life as a martyr.

He is the patron saint of the city of Athens, where his memory has been honored from ancient times. His feast is kept on October 3, a beloved name day for those called Dionysios and Dionysia.
10-3.desc: Holy Hieromartyr Dionysios the Areopagite, first Bishop of Athens.
10-3.name: Dionysios the Areopagite

10-3.bio:
Damaris is named in the Acts of the Apostles among those who believed when Paul preached at the Areopagus in Athens, together with Dionysios the Areopagite.

She is honored as one of the first Christians of Athens, and later tradition regards her as a woman of learning who helped spread the Gospel in the city.
10-3.desc: Saint Damaris of Athens, converted by the preaching of the Apostle Paul on the Areopagus.
10-3.name: Damaris of Athens

10-3.bio:
Rusticus and Eleutherius were a priest and a deacon who accompanied Saint Dionysios in his missionary labors and shared his imprisonment and sufferings.

Tradition relates that they were beheaded together with him, sealing their witness to Christ with their blood.
10-3.desc: Holy Martyrs Rusticus the Presbyter and Eleutherius the Deacon, companions of Saint Dionysios.
10-3.name: Rusticus and Eleutherius

10-3.bio: Theoktistos is commemorated in the Synaxarion among the martyrs of this day. The details of his life are not preserved, but the Church honors his confession of Christ unto death.
10-3.desc: Holy Martyr Theoktistos, commemorated with Saint Dionysios the Areopagite.
10-3.name: Theoktistos the Martyr

10-3.bio:
John was born in Thebes of Egypt and, after ascetic training there, settled in the Choziba ravine near Jericho, where a famous lavra grew up around him. Against his will he was made Bishop of Caesarea in Palestine in the late sixth century.

Longing for silence, he returned to Choziba, where he combated the Eutychian heresy and was known for his gifts of discernment and wonderworking, reposing in peace.
10-3.desc: Saint John the Chozebite, ascetic of the Wadi Qelt and Bishop of Caesarea in Palestine.
10-3.name: John the Chozebite

10-3.bio:
Dionysios was a hieromonk of the Kiev Caves Lavra in the fifteenth century who served as keeper of the caves where the relics of the fathers rest. The Paterikon relates that on Pascha of 1463, when he censed the relics and cried 'Christ is risen,' the departed fathers answered 'Truly He is risen.'

After this he shut himself in a cell as a recluse and lived there in prayer until his repose.
10-3.desc: Venerable Dionysios the Recluse of the Kiev Caves, hieromonk and guardian of the relics of the Far Caves.
10-3.name: Dionysios the Recluse of the Caves

10-30.bio:
Saints Zenobios and Zenobia were brother and sister from Cilicia in Asia Minor. Zenobios, a physician who healed the sick without payment in the name of Christ, became a bishop of the Church; during the persecution under Diocletian he was arrested, and Zenobia freely joined her brother so that she might share his confession and his sufferings.

Together they endured torture and were beheaded, receiving the crown of martyrdom. The two siblings are commemorated together on October 30.
10-30.name: Zenobios and Zenobia

10-30.bio:
Kleopas was one of the two disciples to whom the risen Lord appeared on the road to Emmaus and who recognized Him in the breaking of the bread. Tradition names him the brother of Joseph the Betrothed and numbers him among the Seventy.

He is commemorated on this day together with Saint Joseph, Patriarch of Constantinople, who rejected the Latin union and reposed in peace.
10-30.desc: Holy Apostle Kleopas of the Seventy, to whom the risen Christ appeared on the road to Emmaus, with Saint Joseph, Patriarch of Constantinople.
10-30.name: Kleopas the Apostle

10-30.bio:
Tertius wrote down the Epistle to the Romans at Paul's dictation and became the second Bishop of Iconium. Mark, also called John, was the nephew of Barnabas and Bishop of Apollonia. Justus, called Barsabas, was one of the two put forward to replace Judas and became Bishop of Eleutheropolis. Artemas was Bishop of Lystra.

All four labored for the Gospel and are honored among the Seventy Apostles.
10-30.desc: Holy Apostles Tertius, Mark, Justus and Artemas of the Seventy.
10-30.name: Tertius, Mark, Justus and Artemas

10-30.bio:
Eutropia was a Christian of Alexandria who visited and encouraged the confessors in prison during the persecution of Decius. Arrested for this, she boldly confessed Christ before the governor.

She was tortured and burned, giving up her soul to God around 250.
10-30.name: Eutropia the Martyr

10-30.bio:
Markianos was sent by the Apostle Peter from Antioch to Sicily, where he became the first Bishop of Syracuse and converted many from paganism, living in a cave outside the city.

He was put to death by the Jews and pagans of the city and is honored as the first martyr of Sicily.
10-30.desc: Holy Hieromartyr Markianos, Bishop of Syracuse, disciple of the Apostle Peter.
10-30.name: Markianos of Syracuse

10-30.bio:
These three brothers and their sister were denounced as Christians by their stepmother, who coveted their inheritance, and brought before the governor Lysias at Aegae in Cilicia.

They confessed Christ, endured torture, and were crucified around 285; Neonilla was beheaded after them.
10-30.desc: Holy Martyrs Asterios, Claudius, Neon and their sister Neonilla of Aegae in Cilicia.
10-30.name: Asterios, Claudius, Neon and Neonilla

10-30.bio:
Stephen Milutin ruled Serbia from 1282 to 1321 and built or endowed many churches and monasteries, from Chilandar on Athos to Jerusalem and Constantinople, being honored as the greatest builder among Serbian kings. His brother Dragutin gave up the throne to him and ended his life as the monk Theoktistos.

Their mother Helen, of French origin, founded convents and a school for orphan girls and became a nun before her repose in 1314.
10-30.desc: Saints Stephen Milutin, King of Serbia, his brother Dragutin, called Theoktistos in monasticism, and their mother Helen.
10-30.name: Stephen Milutin, Dragutin and Helen of Serbia

10-31.bio:
St. Stachys was one of the Seventy Apostles, greeted by name by the Apostle Paul in his epistle to the Romans. Tradition relates that he was ordained by the Apostle Andrew as the first Bishop of Byzantium, the city that would one day become Constantinople, where he shepherded the young Christian community and labored in the preaching of the Gospel.

He is honored as the first in the long line of hierarchs of the imperial city. Together with the apostles Apelles, Amplias, Urban, Narcissus, and Aristobulus of the Seventy, he is commemorated on October 31.
10-31.desc: Holy Apostle Stachys, first Bishop of Byzantium.
10-31.name: Stachys the Apostle

10-31.bio:
Epimachos was an ascetic of Mount Pelusium in Egypt who, hearing of the persecution, went down to Alexandria and openly overthrew the idols and confessed Christ.

He was tortured and beheaded around 250; tradition relates that a drop of his blood healed a blind woman standing among the crowd.
10-31.desc: Holy Martyr Epimachos of Pelusium, who suffered at Alexandria.
10-31.name: Epimachos of Egypt

10-31.bio:
Nicholas was born on Chios and in a moment of mental distress uttered the Muslim confession of faith. Recovering, he was tormented by remorse and, after preparing himself by prayer and confession, presented himself before the Turkish judge and proclaimed himself a Christian.

He was beheaded on Chios in 1754, and the Church honors him among the New Martyrs.
10-31.desc: Holy New Martyr Nicholas of Chios, beheaded in 1754.
10-31.name: Nicholas the New Martyr of Chios

10-31.bio:
These apostles are greeted by Saint Paul in the Epistle to the Romans. Apelles became Bishop of Heraclea, Amplias of Odyssopolis, Urban of Macedonia, and Narcissus of Athens; Aristobulus, brother of Barnabas, preached in Britain and died in peace.

They are commemorated together with Stachys, the first Bishop of Byzantium.
10-31.desc: Holy Apostles Apelles, Amplias, Urban, Narcissus and Aristobulus of the Seventy, companions of Saint Stachys.
10-31.greek: Απελλής, Αμπλίας, Ουρβανός, Νάρκισσος και Αριστόβουλος
10-31.name: Apelles, Amplias, Urban, Narcissus and Aristobulus

10-31.bio: Seleukos and Stratonike were a married couple of Cyzicus who confessed Christ together before the pagan authorities. Tradition relates that they endured torture side by side and were put to death, receiving the crown of martyrdom as one.
10-31.desc: Holy Martyrs Seleukos and his wife Stratonike of Cyzicus.
10-31.name: Seleukos and Stratonike

10-31.bio:
Spyridon came to the Kiev Caves as an unlettered man in middle age and was given the obedience of baking the prosphora, which he fulfilled for thirty years while reciting the Psalter by heart. Tradition relates that when the bakery caught fire he carried water in his cloak and put out the flames unharmed.

Nikodemos shared his labor and his prayer, and both reposed in the twelfth century; their relics rest in the Near Caves.
10-31.desc: Venerable Spyridon and Nikodemos, prosphora-bakers of the Kiev Caves.
10-31.name: Spyridon and Nikodemos the Prosphora-Bakers

10-31.bio:
John Kochurov served as a missionary priest in Chicago from 1895 to 1907 under Saint Tikhon, building the cathedral of the Holy Trinity there. He returned to Russia and served at Tsarskoye Selo.

On October 31, 1917, days after the Bolshevik seizure of power, he was dragged from a procession and shot, the first priest to be martyred by the new regime; he was glorified in 1994.
10-31.desc: Holy Hieromartyr John Kochurov, missionary priest in America and first clergy martyr of the Bolshevik revolution.
10-31.name: John Kochurov

10-4.bio:
St. Hierotheos was an Athenian of the apostolic age, converted by the preaching of the Apostle Paul and made a bishop of Athens. Tradition remembers him as a man of deep divine wisdom, the teacher and companion of St. Dionysios the Areopagite, and relates that he was present with the apostles at the Dormition of the Theotokos, where his hymnody moved all who heard him.

He is honored among the first hierarchs of Greece, and is commemorated on October 4.
10-4.desc: Bishop Hierotheos, first Bishop of Athens.
10-4.name: Hierotheus of Athens

10-4.bio:
Domnina, a Christian noblewoman of Antioch, fled with her two daughters to Edessa during the persecution of Diocletian. Her pagan husband pursued them with soldiers and seized them on the road.

Fearing dishonor at the hands of the soldiers, mother and daughters chose to give themselves to the waters of a river rather than lose their purity, and the Church honors them as martyrs. Saint John Chrysostom preached a homily in their praise.
10-4.desc: Holy Martyrs Domnina and her daughters Bernike and Prosdoke of Antioch.
10-4.name: Domnina and her daughters Bernike and Prosdoke

10-4.bio:
John was born at Lampadou in Cyprus to pious parents who had him educated and betrothed. Tradition relates that his intended bride's family poisoned his food when he chose the ascetic life, and he lost his sight.

He bore his blindness with patience and prayer, living in strict asceticism, and reposed at a young age. Many healings took place at his tomb, and a famous monastery bearing his name grew up at Kalopanagiotis.
10-4.desc: Venerable John Lampadistis of Cyprus, the young ascetic and wonderworker of Marathasa.
10-4.name: John Lampadistis

10-4.bio:
Peter was a learned and devout monk of Capitolias beyond the Jordan who was ordained priest by the Bishop of Bostra. Under Arab rule he openly refuted the errors of Islam and preached Christ.

For this he was seized, cruelly mutilated, and finally beheaded and burned, receiving the crown of martyrdom.
10-4.desc: Holy Hieromartyr Peter of Capitolias, priest and monk beheaded by the Saracens.
10-4.name: Peter of Capitolias

10-4.bio:
Audaktos was a nobleman of Ephesus whose daughter Kallisthene was sought in marriage by the emperor Maximian Galerius. Because she refused for Christ's sake, her father was stripped of his rank and possessions, exiled, and finally beheaded.

Kallisthene fled in disguise and lived in hiding until the persecution ended; she then recovered her father's relics and spent the rest of her life in works of charity and prayer.
10-4.desc: Holy Martyr Audaktos and his daughter Saint Kallisthene of Ephesus.
10-4.name: Audaktos and Kallisthene

10-4.bio:
Ammoun was compelled by his relatives to marry, but persuaded his bride to live with him in chastity as brother and sister. After eighteen years they separated by agreement, and he withdrew to the desert of Nitria, where he became the father of a great monastic settlement.

He was a friend of Saint Anthony the Great, who tradition relates saw his soul carried to heaven by angels at the hour of his death in the mid-fourth century.
10-4.desc: Venerable Ammoun of Egypt, founder of the monastic settlement of Nitria.
10-4.name: Ammoun of Egypt

10-5.bio:
St. Charitina was a young Christian woman who suffered martyrdom during the persecutions at the beginning of the fourth century. An orphan raised by a pious guardian, she lived in prayer and purity, and when she was denounced as a Christian she confessed Christ boldly, enduring cruel tortures until she gave her soul to God.

She is numbered among the holy virgin martyrs whose steadfastness put their persecutors to shame. She is commemorated on October 5.
10-5.name: Charitine

10-5.bio:
Methodia was born on the island of Kimolos in 1865 and was married as a young woman. When her husband was lost at sea, she took the monastic habit and enclosed herself in a cell beside the church of the Panagia, living in fasting, vigil and prayer.

Islanders came to her for counsel and healing, and she became a spiritual mother to many. She reposed in 1908 and was glorified by the Ecumenical Patriarchate in 1962.
10-5.desc: Venerable Methodia of Kimolos, the recluse and spiritual mother of the Cyclades.
10-5.name: Methodia of Kimolos

10-5.bio:
Hermogenes is commemorated in the Synaxarion as a hieromartyr and wonderworker who confessed Christ and was put to death for the faith. Tradition relates that he ended his martyrdom by fire.

The details of his life are not preserved, but the Church honors the miracles worked through his intercession.
10-5.name: Hermogenes the Hieromartyr

10-5.bio:
Mamelchtha was a pagan priestess of Artemis in Persia whose sister was a Christian. Moved by a vision of an angel, she came to faith and was baptized by the local bishop.

As she left the baptistery still wearing her white robes, the pagans stoned her to death, and she received the crown of martyrdom in the fourth century.
