10-5.desc: Holy Martyr Mamelchtha of Persia, a former priestess of Artemis who was stoned for Christ.
10-5.name: Mamelchtha of Persia

10-5.bio:
Nothing is known of the earthly life of this monk of Vatopedi. In 1840, when the monastery's ossuary was being rearranged, his relics were found in a kneeling posture, fragrant and holding an icon of the Theotokos.

Because his name was unknown, the fathers called him Eudokimos, one well-pleasing to God, and he has been honored since as a newly-revealed saint of the Holy Mountain.
10-5.desc: Venerable Eudokimos the Newly-Revealed of Vatopedi Monastery on Mount Athos.
10-5.name: Eudokimos of Vatopedi

10-5.bio:
John Mavropous was one of the most learned men of eleventh-century Constantinople, teacher of Michael Psellos and a counsellor of the emperor Constantine IX Monomachos. He was later consecrated Metropolitan of Euchaita in Pontus.

He composed many canons and hymns still in use, and tradition credits him with establishing the common feast of the Three Hierarchs on January 30.
10-5.desc: Saint John Mavropous, Bishop of Euchaita, hymnographer and teacher of Constantinople.
10-5.name: John Mavropous of Euchaita

10-6.bio:
St. Thomas, called the Twin, was one of the Twelve Apostles. Absent when the risen Christ first appeared to the disciples, he said he would not believe unless he touched the wounds of the Lord; eight days later Christ invited him to do so, and Thomas confessed Him as Lord and God — the clearest confession of the divinity of Christ in the Gospels.

According to tradition Thomas carried the Gospel east as far as India, where ancient Christian communities trace their origin to his preaching, and where he died a martyr. He is commemorated on October 6 and on the first Sunday after Pascha.
10-6.name: Thomas the Apostle

10-6.bio:
Erotheis was a Christian maiden who confessed Christ before the pagan authorities and refused to sacrifice to idols. Tradition relates that she was cast into a fire and gave up her soul to God unharmed in faith.

The Church honors her among the virgin martyrs of the early centuries.
10-6.desc: Holy Martyr Erotheis, who was burned for her confession of Christ.
10-6.name: Erotheis the Martyr

10-6.bio:
Makarios was born at Kios in Bithynia; his father had converted to Islam and pressed him to do the same. He fled to Mount Athos and became a monk at the Skete of Saint Anne.

Seized with the desire for martyrdom, he returned home and openly confessed Christ before the Turkish judge. After imprisonment and torture he was beheaded at Prousa in 1590.
10-6.desc: Holy New Monk-Martyr Makarios of Kios in Bithynia, beheaded at Prousa in 1590.
10-6.name: Makarios of Kios

10-6.bio:
Kendeas came from Germany, or according to another account from Palestine, and lived as a hermit in the Jordan desert before sailing to Cyprus. He settled in a cave near the village of Avgorou, where he lived in fasting and prayer.

Tradition relates that he worked many miracles, bringing forth a spring of water by his prayer, and that healings continued at his tomb after his repose.
10-6.desc: Venerable Kendeas the Wonderworker of Cyprus, hermit of Avgorou.
10-6.name: Kendeas the Wonderworker

10-6.bio:
Born in 1797 in Siberia, the priest John Veniaminov volunteered for the mission to the Aleutian Islands, where he learned the native tongue, created an alphabet, and translated the Scriptures and services. As Bishop Innocent he founded churches and schools across Alaska and eastern Siberia.

In 1868 he became Metropolitan of Moscow, where he established the Orthodox Missionary Society. He reposed in 1879 and was glorified in 1977.
10-6.desc: Saint Innocent Veniaminov, Metropolitan of Moscow, Enlightener of the Aleuts and Apostle to America.
10-6.name: Innocent of Alaska

10-6.bio:
Gregory was born in the eighth century to a noble Georgian family and was raised at the royal court, but chose the monastic life. He founded the monastery of Khandzta in the wilderness of Klarjeti and many other communities.

He composed a monastic rule for his monks and reposed in 861 after a long life, being honored as the architect of Georgian monasticism.
10-6.desc: Venerable Gregory of Khandzta, founder of monasteries and father of monasticism in Georgia.
10-6.name: Gregory of Khandzta

10-7.bio:
Saints Sergius and Bacchus were high-ranking officers in the Roman army at the end of the third century, secretly Christians and beloved of the emperor. When their faith was discovered they refused to sacrifice to the idols; stripped of their rank, they were paraded in mockery and cruelly tortured. Bacchus died under the blows, and Sergius was afterward beheaded in Syria.

The city of Resafa, where Sergius suffered, became a great center of pilgrimage bearing his name. The two friends and fellow soldiers of Christ are commemorated together on October 7.
10-7.name: Sergios and Vakchos

10-7.bio:
Polychronios was the son of a farmer in Gamphanitos who worked as a vine-dresser in Constantinople and lived in fasting and prayer. Tradition relates that his master, seeing his holiness, gave him gold with which he built a church; he was ordained priest and was present at the First Ecumenical Council.

In the reign of Constantius he was seized by Arians and cut down at the holy table while celebrating the Divine Liturgy.
10-7.desc: Holy Hieromartyr Polychronios the Presbyter, slain by the Arians at the altar.
10-7.name: Polychronios the Hieromartyr

10-7.bio:
John came from Egypt with thirty-six companions and settled in Crete, where they were joined by others until they numbered ninety-nine. They lived in caves near Akrotiri, and John, their leader, was known for his continual prayer and gift of wonderworking.

Tradition relates that in his old age, crawling on all fours from weakness, he was mistaken for an animal and shot by a hunter, and that he forgave the man before reposing.
10-7.desc: Venerable John the Hermit and the ninety-eight God-bearing Fathers who lived in asceticism with him in Crete.
10-7.name: John the Hermit and the 98 Fathers of Crete

10-7.bio:
Caesarius, a deacon from Africa, came to Terracina and openly rebuked the pagan custom of casting a youth from a cliff in honor of Apollo. With the priest Julian he was imprisoned and tortured.

Both were sewn into a sack and thrown into the sea, receiving the crown of martyrdom in the first or early second century.
10-7.desc: Holy Martyrs Julian the Presbyter and Caesarius the Deacon, who suffered at Terracina in Italy.
10-7.name: Julian and Caesarius of Terracina

10-7.bio:
Leontios held consular rank and was a Christian. Tradition relates that he confessed Christ openly and distributed his goods to the poor before his death.

The Synaxarion honors him among the martyrs of this day, though the details of his sufferings are not preserved.
10-7.desc: Holy Martyr Leontios the Consul, who gave up his soul in confession of Christ.
10-7.name: Leontios the Hypatikos

10-8.bio:
St. Pelagia was a celebrated actress of Antioch, renowned for her beauty and wealth, who was brought to compunction by the preaching of a holy bishop. She was baptized, gave her riches to the poor, and departed secretly to Jerusalem, where she lived in a cell on the Mount of Olives in strict asceticism, unknown to all until her repose.

She is honored as a model of true repentance, showing that no life is beyond the reach of the mercy of God. She is commemorated on October 8.
10-8.name: Pelagia

10-8.bio:
Pelagia was a fifteen-year-old Christian of Antioch during the persecution under Numerian. When soldiers came to seize her, she asked leave to change her garments and, praying, threw herself from the roof of the house to preserve her purity.

Saint John Chrysostom and Saint Ambrose both praised her as a martyr for her chastity.
10-8.desc: Holy Virgin Martyr Pelagia of Antioch, who chose death rather than dishonor.
10-8.name: Pelagia the Virgin of Antioch

10-8.bio:
Thais was a woman of Alexandria who lived a life of sin until the abba Paphnutios came to her disguised as a customer and spoke to her of the judgment of God. Struck with compunction, she burned her possessions in the public square.

She was enclosed in a cell in a women's monastery for three years of repentance, and tradition relates that a vision showed her forgiveness; she reposed in peace soon after.
10-8.desc: Venerable Thais of Egypt, the penitent who became a great ascetic.
10-8.name: Thais of Egypt

10-8.bio:
Born John in Eski Zagora of Bulgaria, he was raised in piety but in a moment of weakness he had once professed Islam under pressure. Repenting bitterly, he went to Mount Athos and became a monk named Ignatios under the elders of the Skete of the Forerunner.

He returned to Constantinople and confessed Christ before the Turkish court, and was hanged in 1814; his relics were taken to Athos.
10-8.desc: Holy New Monk-Martyr Ignatios of Stara Zagora, hanged at Constantinople in 1814.
10-8.name: Ignatios the New Martyr of Bulgaria

10-8.bio:
Tryphon was born in the mid-sixteenth century in the Mezen region and became a monk in Perm, where he preached to the pagan Ostyaks and Voguls. He later founded the Dormition monastery at Vyatka and served as its archimandrite.

He reposed in 1612 and is venerated as the enlightener and wonderworker of Vyatka.
10-8.desc: Venerable Tryphon, Archimandrite of Vyatka, wonderworker of the Russian north.
10-8.name: Tryphon of Vyatka

10-8.bio:
Philip was Bishop of Gortyna, the ancient capital of Crete, in the second century and is praised by Saint Dionysios of Corinth for the steadfastness of his church.

He wrote a treatise against the heresy of Marcion and is honored among the early fathers of the Church of Crete.
10-8.desc: Saint Philip, Bishop of Gortyna in Crete, apologist of the second century.
10-8.name: Philip of Gortyna

10-9.bio:
St. James the son of Alphaeus was one of the Twelve Apostles chosen by the Lord, named in each of the Gospel lists of the Twelve. After Pentecost he went forth, as the apostles did, to preach the Gospel among the nations, and tradition relates that he ended his labors as a martyr for Christ.

The synaxaria preserve little of the details of his journeys, but the Church honors him among the foundational Twelve upon whose preaching she is built. He is commemorated on October 9.
10-9.desc: Holy Apostle James son of Alpheus.
10-9.name: James the Apostle of Alphaeus

10-9.bio:
Andronikos was a goldsmith of Antioch in the fifth century, married to Athanasia; they gave a third of their earnings to the poor and lived in piety. When both of their children died on the same day, they resolved to give themselves wholly to God.

Andronikos entered a monastery in Egypt and Athanasia a convent; tradition relates that many years later they met again on the road, she disguised as a monk, and lived as ascetics side by side without her revealing herself until her death.
10-9.desc: Venerable Andronikos and his wife Athanasia of Antioch, who embraced the ascetic life together.
10-9.name: Andronikos and Athanasia

10-9.bio:
Abraham was called by God to leave his homeland and go to the land of promise, and received the promise that in his seed all nations would be blessed. He is honored as the father of the faithful for his obedience, above all in his readiness to offer his son Isaac.

Lot, his nephew, lived righteously among the wicked of Sodom and was delivered by angels before the city's destruction.
10-9.desc: Righteous Forefather Abraham, friend of God, and his nephew Lot the Righteous.
10-9.name: Abraham and Lot the Righteous

10-9.bio:
Poplia was a widow of Antioch who raised her son John as a Christian and became a deaconess, gathering a choir of virgins about her. When the emperor Julian the Apostate passed by, she led them in singing psalms mocking the idols.

The emperor had her beaten, but she did not cease, and she reposed in peace in the fourth century honored as a confessor.
10-9.desc: Saint Poplia the Confessor, deaconess of Antioch, who defied Julian the Apostate.
10-9.name: Poplia the Confessor

10-9.bio:
Born Leo in Galatia, he served in the imperial army under the iconoclast emperor Theophilos and was taken captive by the Arabs. Delivered from prison through prayer, he vowed himself to God and became a monk with the name Peter.

He lived as a hermit on Mount Olympus in Bithynia and later near Constantinople, reposing in peace in the ninth century.
10-9.desc: Venerable Peter of Galatia, the soldier who became a hermit.
10-9.name: Peter the Former Soldier

10-9.bio:
Born Vasily Belavin in 1865, he served as Bishop of the Aleutians and North America, establishing dioceses and the first Orthodox seminary in the United States. In 1917 he was elected Patriarch of Moscow, the first after two centuries.

He led the Church through the Bolshevik persecution, enduring imprisonment, and reposed in 1925. He was glorified in 1989; this day commemorates his glorification.
10-9.desc: Saint Tikhon, Patriarch of Moscow and Enlightener of North America, confessor under the Bolsheviks.
10-9.name: Tikhon Patriarch of Moscow
